Chapter 7: The Scope of Harm — Suffering Across Species
When we think about the harm that comes with existence, it’s natural to focus on human lives first. But really, our world is full of sentient beings, each with their own ability to feel pain and joy. So the question of harm? It stretches way beyond just us.
Picture a child stepping into an animal shelter. They’re drawn in by the abandoned dogs and cats—seeing fear in their eyes, the marks of past neglect, and that quiet longing for comfort. In that moment, the child realizes something profound: suffering isn’t just a human experience. It’s part of life for every creature that can feel.
Most people do care about animals—at least in theory. We get upset when we hear about cruelty, and we try not to cause harm when we can help it. But here’s something to really think about: when it comes to existence itself, the same logic applies. Every sentient creature that’s brought into the world faces the risk of suffering—and none of them get to choose.
The natural world, for all its beauty, is filled with pain. Wild animals deal with hunger, disease, injuries, and, eventually, death. Even in the best of circumstances, their lives are often short and full of hardship. So the harm that comes with existing? It’s not just a human issue—it’s something all sentient life has to deal with.
Some folks argue that animal suffering is just part of nature—something we have to accept. But just accepting it doesn’t make the pain any less real, or any less serious. The fact that suffering is common doesn’t mean it should be ignored.
As the child leaves the shelter, they carry a heavy feeling. They start to see that the question of harm is bigger than they ever imagined. It isn’t just about people, or even about the choices of individuals. It’s about how the entire world is set up—and the risks that every new life faces, right from the start.
And when we look at it from this wider angle, the moral challenge becomes even deeper. If it’s wrong to force suffering on humans without their consent, isn’t it just as wrong to do it to animals? The harm of coming into existence crosses all species—and maybe, it’s time we rethink how we value life itself.
